prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 3 columns and 3 rows of equal 9:16 panels, 8 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a clean, simple line drawing: uniform thin black outlines on a plain white background, with no shading, hatching, grey tones, colour or texture. Each panel has a thin black border, with plain white gutters between the panels. Location: The Quinn family mansion, living room, Day, soft natural daylight from the tall windows.
Image 1: the character sheet of Cassie (23)
Image 2: the character sheet of Natalie (25)
Image 3: the character sheet of Lauren (50)
Image 4: the location The Quinn family mansion, living room, with no people
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image: the hairstyle, build and outfit in outline. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location image only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location image, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: The camera stays on the near side of the coffee table, facing the back wall, windows at frame left. Natalie stands just inside the right-wall doorway at frame right, beside the empty front-right armchair, turned back toward the room. She holds the flat hospital statement at her side, her bag hangs from her shoulder, and her eyes are glassy without tears. Cassie stands at the right side of the empty front-left armchair, on the coffee-table side, facing Natalie toward frame right, arms relaxed at her sides. Lauren sits forward on the sofa's right end, turned toward Cassie, hands still in her lap. George sits on the sofa's left end; every shot is framed to exclude the sofa's left end, so he stays out of frame.
Panel 1: Medium shot, two-shot, eye-level, locked-off from the near side, facing the right wall. Behind both of them are the pale grey right wall and the open doorway; the back wall with the sofa lies entirely beyond frame left. Cassie is on frame left by the front-left armchair and Natalie on frame right by the right-wall doorway. Cassie takes a slow half step toward Natalie and tilts her head with a sweet, poisonous smile, her hands at her sides. Natalie faces her with a wary frown, no smile.
Panel 2: Medium shot, low angle from the near side facing the back wall on Lauren at the sofa's right end, slight push in, framed on her chest and face. Behind her are the upper back wall, the edge of the framed painting and the potted fig at the right of the arch. The sofa's left end lies beyond frame left and the right-wall doorway beyond frame right. Lauren sits up straighter and beams proudly toward Cassie, her hands resting still in her lap.
Panel 3: Close-up, eye-level, locked-off from the near side facing the right wall on Natalie's face as she faces frame left toward Cassie. Behind her is only the pale grey right wall beside the doorway frame. Natalie's eyes widen in disbelief and she draws her head back, her lips parted in shock, no smile. Her hands and the statement stay below frame.
Panel 4: Medium shot, over-the-shoulder shot from the near side behind Cassie's right shoulder onto Natalie at the right-wall doorway, handheld, facing the right wall. Behind Natalie are the pale grey right wall and the open doorway frame; the back wall with the sofa lies beyond frame left. Natalie shakes her head slightly and frowns at Cassie, no smile. Cassie's shoulder and curls fill the foreground.
Panel 5: Medium close-up, eye-level, locked-off from the near side by the front-right armchair on Cassie beside the front-left armchair. The camera faces the left wall, so behind her the sheer-curtained windows fill the background and the sofa lies beyond frame right. Cassie shrugs one shoulder and pops her glossy lips.
Panel 6: Medium shot, low angle on Cassie beside the coffee table, slow orbit on the near side from her front to her right side while the camera keeps facing the left-wall windows. Behind her are the sheer-curtained windows, the upper wall and the unlit chandelier; the sofa stays beyond frame right and below frame. Cassie wrinkles her nose in disgust and tosses her head so her platinum curls swing over her shoulder, her hands at her sides.
Panel 7: Medium shot, eye-level, locked-off from the near side facing the right wall on Natalie standing by the doorway. Behind her are only the pale grey right wall and the doorway frame; Cassie and the sofa lie beyond frame left. Natalie recoils a half step with wide eyes, shakes her head and presses her lips tight in refusal, no smile. Her hands and the flat statement hang at her side below frame. Cassie is off screen.
Panel 8: Medium close-up, eye-level, quick cut from the near side facing the back wall to Lauren at the sofa's right end, framed on her face and shoulders. Behind her are the sofa back and the potted fig at the right of the arch. The sofa's left end lies beyond frame left and the right-wall doorway beyond frame right. Lauren nods firmly with a thin red smile, her hands still in her lap.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering, shading or colour.
